newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Prince Charles stays at historic Gorbachev dacha.
newsitem.headline: Prince Charles stays at historic Gorbachev dacha.

text.p: Britain's Prince Charles was spending Tuesday night in the house where Mikhail Gorbachev was kept prisoner during a hardline coup attempt in August 1991, British officials said.

The prince will be the first Western dignitary to visit the former Soviet president's "dacha" -- a Slavonic word for a country home -- which was once in Soviet territory but is now in Ukraine's Crimean peninsula.
Gorbachev was on holiday at the Foros dacha -- in fact a palatial multistorey palace on the Crimea's southern coast -- when the coup was launched on August 19.

First his telephones were cut off and the estate sealed off. A group of the conspirators flew down to try and persuade him to join their bid to stop a treaty which was to devolve more power to the 15 republics which made up the Soviet Union.
He refused and was held there incommunicado until the coup collapsed on August 21. It hastened the breakup of the Soviet Union which happened four months later.
Prince Charles is in Ukraine on a three-day visit and will leave for Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan, on Wednesday, British officials accompanying him said.
The prince on Tuesday visited a military cemetery where lie buried British dead from the 1853-56 Crimean War between tsarist Russia and a joint British, French and Turkish force.
More than 500 British cavalry, many from aristocratic families, were killed nearby at the battle of Inkerman on November 5, 1854.

Charles also visited a Crimean Tatar family in the town of Bakhchisarai, and toured the palace of the powerful Crimean Khans who ruled the peninsula as vassals of Turkey until Russia conquered it in the 1780s.
